results.summary_before: This design is a cubic polynomial sampler (difference engine) with an SPI request interface and step/dir output, written in DSLX and compiled with Google XLS. It samples a cubic polynomial using forward differences and outputs step and direction signals for a stepper motor driver. The design accepts 64-bit requests over SPI containing polynomial coefficients and sample count. It requires an SPI master and optionally a stepper driver, and can also be built for an FPGA board.

results.summary_before: The Fed Model is a hardware implementation of a Federal Reserve rate-cycle risk model that counts rate cuts and signals when to exit the market. It uses event strobes for rate cuts, hikes, and months, and outputs the investment decision along with internal state. The design supports two model variants (F1 and F2) selectable at runtime, with configurable cut threshold. It is tested via a cocotb suite against a Python reference model and requires no external hardware beyond strobe drivers.

results.summary_before: RTFCE is a multi-context temporal latency monitor that measures time between configurable start and end events and classifies each measurement as PASS, EARLY, or TIMEOUT. It supports three independent contexts sharing a single classification datapath via selectable fixed-priority or round-robin arbitration. The design includes a near-miss diagnostic and is fully configurable via a bidirectional bus. It is tested with a cocotb regression and requires no external hardware.

results.summary_before: This project implements a 4-iteration rotation mode CORDIC algorithm that computes the sine and cosine of a 6-bit angle. The angle is loaded via the input pins, and the result is displayed on a 7-segment display, with a DONE flag on the decimal point. It requires a 7-segment display for output and switches or a microcontroller to provide the input angle and start signal. The design is notable for fitting a CORDIC calculator into a single Tiny Tapeout tile.
